about: Everything that slowed, surprised or annoyed an agent or a person while working on blaze, however slightly, written down when it happens (rule record-annoyances). A row is a lead for guard-the-cause: the fix is to remove the cause, then set the row's state. Rows are never deleted; a fixed one keeps its state and the commit.

annoyances.where: the task's premise: the profile's size
annoyances.what: The brief said the profile directory's 551 MB was spans, waits, samples and per-flush files. 516 MiB of it was one file, `flight-<pid>.map`, the flight recorder's mapping with all 256 rings' stores reserved up front; the Parquet history was 17 MB and `why.ledger` 17 MB. `du` of `profile/` says one number for three different things.
annoyances.cost: the first plan (aggregate waits) aimed at 3% of the bytes
annoyances.cause: nothing reports the history's directory by what is in it (the mapping, the ledger, each table)
annoyances.workaround: listed the directory by table with a one-line awk
annoyances.state: fixed for the mapping in 31664bef18 (reserved as handed out); a `blaze debug disk` that says each part is open

annoyances.where: blaze-profile: the mapping's reservation on macOS
annoyances.what: `F_PREALLOCATE` asked with `F_ALLOCATECONTIG` alone succeeds with whatever contiguous run it found: a 3.4 MiB ask came back with 20 KiB reserved and no error, so the mapping's promise (no SIGBUS on a full disk) held only because the 516 MiB ask happened to fail and fall through to `F_ALLOCATEALL`.
annoyances.cost: found only because the new test's oracle checks the blocks the file holds
annoyances.cause: the code never read `fst_bytesalloc`
annoyances.workaround: none needed
annoyances.state: fixed in 31664bef18: all or nothing, and the bytes given are checked

annoyances.where: blaze-profile's tests under cargo on macOS
annoyances.what: Three tests fail on the untouched tip of all-1111 (65fafef399): `batches::tests::names_given_on_many_threads_read_back_from_parquet_as_recorded` every time, alone too (two of five threads' spans missing); `history::tests::past_the_cap_the_oldest_files_go_first` and `history::tests::a_pinned_reader_keeps_retired_files_until_it_lets_go` (and once `past_the_cap_a_build_goes_whole`) only when the suite runs in parallel, passing alone.
annoyances.cost: a baseline worktree and three extra runs to tell them from my changes
annoyances.cause: not looked for: the cap tests share something across tests in one process (the pins directory or the reaper's timing)
annoyances.workaround: ran each alone and on a detached worktree of the base
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.where: blaze-cargo's tests under cargo on macOS
annoyances.what: `cli::tests::every_command_suggested_is_one` fails (`serve` is in COMMANDS and is no command) and `serve::why::tests::a_changed_key_part_is_named_by_subject_and_survives_a_restore` expects a torn third record to be called `record 1` where the code says `record 2`. Both fail the same way on the untouched tip of all-1111 (65fafef399), run alone.
annoyances.cost: a baseline build of blaze-cargo's tests to tell them from this lane's changes
annoyances.cause: not looked for
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: `du` counts a clone's blocks once a file: the store's `placed/*.derived` files read as 450 MB and hold 9.6 MB of their own, so a home's `du` total can be several times what it holds, and the script every lane was given (`/tmp/blaze-fresh.sh`) reports `du`.
annoyances.cost: one wrong conclusion nearly drawn (that the store had tripled)
annoyances.cause: `du` has no notion of shared extents
annoyances.workaround: wrote a script that asks `ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE` per file (`/private/tmp/blaze-disk-scripts/private.py`, gone with the lane)
annoyances.state: open: the measuring script should say private bytes beside `du`'s

annoyances.what: `stat -f %z` failed inside a script because GNU `stat` from nix is first on PATH; `/usr/bin/stat` had to be spelled out. The same cause as A1.
annoyances.cost: minutes
annoyances.cause: two toolchains on one PATH
annoyances.workaround: spell `/usr/bin/stat`
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.where: blaze: `blaze debug sql` in a fresh home
annoyances.what: The first `blaze debug sql` in a home downloads DuckDB into `<home>/v2/duckdb` (55 MB), a copy a home, though it is a pinned binary named by its version and hash.
annoyances.cost: 55 MB a home, and the first query waits for the download
annoyances.cause: the tool directory is under the home's state, not the machine's shared directory
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: An idle daemon still wakes its loop every 50 ms, its profile drain every 50 ms and its stop guard every 100 ms, each a span, and plots ten counters every 50 ms: 45 span rows and 235 counter rows a second with nothing happening, 0.15 MB a minute of history after this lane's changes (1.2 MB before).
annoyances.cost: about 220 MB a day of history for a daemon left running, which the cap now takes back first
annoyances.cause: polling loops where a wait on an event would do, and gauges written whether or not they changed
annoyances.workaround: the cap retires rows of no build before any build's (e8aec1d91a)
annoyances.state: open: the ticks themselves are the runtime's

annoyances.what: The linked executable is in the build directory twice, each with its own blocks (`debug/hello` and `debug/build/hello/<id>/out/hello`, 23.2 MB each on disk, 158.5 MB long), and so is its `.dSYM` (8.1 MB each): 31 MB of hello-world's 63 MB build directory is a second copy.
annoyances.cost: 31 MB a program
annoyances.cause: each path is placed from the store as its own file and patched on its own
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: open: one file and a hard link, or the patch room gone (launcher.md step 5)

annoyances.what: `annoyances.json` is not on `all-1111` (it is on `film-1111`), so every lane cut from all-1111 adds the file and they will conflict add/add when merged.
annoyances.cost: a merge conflict a lane
annoyances.cause: the file was started on a branch the lanes were not cut from
annoyances.workaround: rows here have ids `disk-1` up so they can be appended
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.where: cargo: one CARGO_TARGET_DIR for two worktrees
annoyances.what: A second worktree of the same tree built into the same target directory (to get a baseline of the tests) left its `blaze-profile` there, and cargo then took it as fresh for the lane's worktree: blaze-cargo's tests failed to compile against the base's blaze-profile (`cannot find value DETAIL_VAR`), with nothing saying the artifact was another tree's. The first sign was an empty result file.
annoyances.cost: one wrong test run and 20 minutes
annoyances.cause: the unit's directory under `debug/build/<package>/<hash>` has the same hash for both worktrees, and freshness is by modification time
annoyances.workaround: removed the base worktree and touched the changed crates' roots
annoyances.state: open: a baseline needs its own target directory, which the disk had no room for

annoyances.where: blaze-cargo's tests under cargo on macOS
annoyances.what: About 50 of `serve::tests` fail on the base and on the lane alike, a different set each run: `the store's pool of 4096 windows of 1073741824 bytes could not reserve its pages: reserving 4398046511104 bytes of address space failed`. Each test's store reserves 4 TiB of address space and six tests at once (and what earlier ones leave reserved) pass what the process can have.
annoyances.cost: the suite cannot say whether a change to the daemon broke anything; this lane ran its own modules' tests by name
annoyances.cause: the pool's reservation is sized for a daemon, and a test's store takes the same
annoyances.workaround: ran `serve::log`, `serve::flightrec`, `serve::said`, `serve::why`, `serve::observe`, `serve::settings` by name
annoyances.state: open (the daemon-memory lane's)

annoyances.what: A unit started with `systemd-run` has no PATH that holds bash, git or curl: `systemd-run ... bash -c ...` fails with `bash: command not found`, and the failure is only in the unit's own log.
annoyances.cost: ten minutes: the first setup unit did nothing and the next command read an empty log
annoyances.cause: the image's binaries are on the login shell's PATH (nix profile paths), not on systemd's default
annoyances.workaround: `systemd-run -E PATH="$PATH" -E HOME=/root /usr/bin/bash ...`
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: `pkill -f "blaze-engine serve"` inside `ix shell vm -- bash -c '...'` kills the bash that runs it, since its own command line holds the pattern; everything after it in the script silently does not run.
annoyances.cost: one measurement run that never started, found twenty minutes later
annoyances.cause: pattern matching on full command lines
annoyances.workaround: `pgrep -f "engine serv[e]" | xargs -r kill`
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.where: blaze: `blaze debug inspect`, the memory section
annoyances.what: `memory.tags` is each tag's blaze-mem bytes only: on a daemon of 5.8 GiB resident they summed to 2.5 GiB, with nothing on the global heap (1.8 GiB live) or on what was freed and kept (1.9 GiB). The full split was only in a line of serve.log written every 30 s while the daemon works.
annoyances.cost: an hour before the first true table
annoyances.cause: the section predates the heap per tag
annoyances.workaround: none needed
annoyances.state: fixed on mem2-1111 (9137787c00: heap by holder with what its pages hold, regions, kept; schema 2)

annoyances.where: blaze: heap samples in a cargo-built binary
annoyances.what: `memory_sites` and `held_samples` named `__rustc::__rust_alloc` and `<Counting<Heaps> as GlobalAlloc>::realloc` as the call site of 90% of the bytes: the plumbing list knew the allocator shims only by the names blaze gives them.
annoyances.cost: the attribution table could not be made until it was fixed
annoyances.cause: a list of names with no test on a binary the system linker made
annoyances.workaround: none needed
annoyances.state: fixed on mem2-1111 (276ba7e15a)

annoyances.what: Every memory view is of a build at its footprint's peak. An idle daemon's question (what do you hold now, after the builds) had no view: `blaze explain memory` picks the last build with memory rows, often a 2 ms store task, and prints empty tables.
annoyances.cost: several hand-written queries
annoyances.cause: the views were made for the self-build's peak
annoyances.workaround: `blaze explain memory_held_now`; the idle line in serve.log (`idle: the kept front end of ... holds`)
annoyances.state: fixed on mem2-1111 (276ba7e15a, and the idle line)

annoyances.where: blaze-engine: mimalloc and transparent huge pages
annoyances.what: `huge.rs` set `mi_option_large_os_pages` from BLAZE_HUGE_PAGES to choose whether mimalloc is on transparent huge pages. In mimalloc 3 that option is hugetlb only; `MADV_HUGEPAGE` is under `allow_thp`, on by default, and the first arena is mapped before `main`. So BLAZE_HUGE_PAGES never decided it, `BLAZE_HUGE_PAGES=off` left mimalloc's arenas on huge pages only because the kernel-wide opt-out covers unadvised memory, and the comment's measurement was of something else.
annoyances.cost: one wrong build and measurement, and a wrong belief about what the setting does
annoyances.cause: an option's name carried over from mimalloc 2; nothing checked the mapping's flags
annoyances.workaround: libmimalloc-sys's `no_thp` feature is the one switch (build time); measured, it is 1.7 GiB less resident and a body edit 17% slower, so it is not set
annoyances.state: the module's docs are true on mem2-1111 (0d7549c6e0); the choice itself is open to anyone who measures bare metal

annoyances.where: blaze-mem and blaze-cas: give-backs nobody calls
annoyances.what: `frame::trim_spare` says it is "what a worker does when it goes idle after a burst" and `Store::evict_pool` says it is "what the daemon's ceiling guard asks before it gives up"; neither had a caller outside its crate's tests. An idle daemon kept 278 MiB of frame shelves and 68 MiB of pool pages for good.
annoyances.cost: found only by the table; the comments said it was done
annoyances.cause: the function landed, the call site did not, and a doc comment in the present tense reads as built
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: trim_spare is called by the idle give-back on mem2-1111; evict_pool still has no caller (open)

annoyances.where: cargo build of blaze (the measuring binary)
annoyances.what: A cargo build prints several hundred `cargo::missing_lints_inheritance` and rustc warnings (291 in blaze-cargo alone) before any error; a filter for `^error` with context was drowned and reported a failed build as having no error.
annoyances.cost: one build misread
annoyances.cause: the tree is linted by blaze, so cargo's own warnings are nobody's
annoyances.workaround: `RUSTFLAGS="--cap-lints allow"` and grep `^error` in the kept log
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: `body edit + run` run back to back is bimodal on every binary, the base included: 100 to 120 ms or 280 to 340 ms, with one of forty past a second. Each edit's build is followed by about 0.7 s of work after the answer (`store kept front end`, the release), and an edit that arrives inside it waits. Medians of 15 runs swing between 125 and 300 ms for the same binary.
annoyances.cost: three rounds of measurement before any row could be compared; the lane compares the 25th percentile and a row with a pause before each edit
annoyances.cause: the next request waits for the work the last one left; not looked into further by this lane
annoyances.workaround: read p25 and min, and the rows with a pause
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: `#![blaze::sans_io]` at the top of a module file does not compile in blaze-cargo under cargo (custom inner attributes are unstable; blaze-query enables the feature, blaze-cargo does not).
annoyances.cost: one failed build
annoyances.cause: the feature gate is per crate
annoyances.workaround: `#[blaze::sans_io]` on the `mod` line
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: A one-line body edit of hello-world allocates and frees about 95 MiB of the global heap: `CompiledFunction::clone` 27 MiB, the linker's `file::fill` 20, `Build::patch_lists` 13, `beside::DebugWrite::apply` 8, `codegen::debug_side` 7.5 (alloc_samples by site, eight edits). The warm loop is meant to allocate nothing there (docs/v2/plan/design/memory.md).
annoyances.cost: it is why mimalloc on base pages is 17% slower an edit (each build takes the freed pages again a 4 KiB fault at a time), so it is what keeps 1.0 GiB of huge-page slack on every Linux daemon; and it is edit time on any pages
annoyances.cause: the edit's link and the walk copy whole-program tables
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: open (codegen and link lanes)

annoyances.what: A command that starts with `sleep N;` is refused, and a foreground wait loop is moved to the background after three minutes, so waiting for a four-minute measurement on a VM takes two or three tool calls.
annoyances.cost: a minute each time, about fifteen times
annoyances.cause: the harness's rule against sleeping
annoyances.workaround: an `until ... do sleep 20; done` loop, read when its notification comes
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: A forced collect (`mi_collect(true)`) purges nothing once `purge_delay` is 0 (`mi_arenas_try_purge` returns at `delay <= 0`), and with a delay a page a thread frees after the last forced purge stays scheduled until the next. Keeping freed pages for the next edit and purging them when idle therefore left 1.1 to 1.5 GiB on an idle daemon, and made an edit 3.5 s after the last 28% slower (154.6 ms against 121.0), which this lane did not explain.
annoyances.cost: four commits made and taken out again, about three hours with their measurements
annoyances.cause: the delay is one process-wide option read at each free and at each purge
annoyances.workaround: purge at once, as before
annoyances.state: open: why a rested edit is slower on pages kept warm is not known

annoyances.what: hir-ty-codegen's unit tests did not compile on all-1111: `wasm.rs`'s test module called `iconst`, `iadd` and 28 more without `InstBuilder` in scope and `FunctionBuilder::finalize` without its argument (32 errors). No unit test of the crate could build, the edit fuzzer (`v2/edits.rs`) among them.
annoyances.cost: twenty minutes; and the fuzzer that holds incremental builds to clean ones was not running for anyone
annoyances.cause: a test module written by a lane that could not build it; nothing compiles test targets before a merge
annoyances.workaround: fixed here in three lines (the import, the two `finalize` arguments)
annoyances.state: fixed on revisions-1111; open: the gate should compile every test target (`cargo test --no-run`) of the crates a merge touches

annoyances.what: A `cargo test --no-run` of another package, run while a 6-minute suite was queued behind cargo's lock, relinked `target/release/blaze` (a `#[cfg(test)]` edit in hir-ty-codegen changes the lib's source file). A client of the new binary then told the daemon of the old one `is another build of blaze ... stopping it and starting this one`.
annoyances.cost: one suite run I had to reason about before trusting, and a rule for the rest of the session: no cargo while a real-driver suite runs
annoyances.cause: the test target's `CARGO_BIN_EXE_blaze` is the one file every build rewrites; a daemon is tied to the exact binary
annoyances.workaround: never build while the suite runs; `BLAZE_REVISIONS_BLAZE=<a copy>` runs the suite on a binary nothing rewrites
annoyances.state: open: the suite could copy the binary into its root first

annoyances.what: `blaze stop` answers before the daemon's process has exited. A daemon started at once at the same home path (the old home renamed away) ended with exit 1, `USAGE: its command line was refused ... while finding its build and its state`, once in a 21-case run.
annoyances.cost: one false failure of a clean build, 15 minutes to find
annoyances.cause: stop is acknowledged before exit; what the second daemon tripped on I did not find (its log was replaced)
annoyances.workaround: the harness waits for the pid to be gone after `blaze stop`
annoyances.state: open: unknown cause; the harness works around it

annoyances.what: Which build is answered by the no-op lane is easy to get wrong from outside: only the third identical request in a row is (the first builds, the second walks and is kept), any difference in arguments (`--message-format=json`) or environment counts as another request, and `build` then `run` then `build` never reaches it. Nothing in a build's output says why a walk was not answered.
annoyances.cost: three wrong expectations in the first cases, 30 minutes
annoyances.cause: by design (docs/cargo.md, "A build with nothing changed"), but silent
annoyances.workaround: `"build_id": null` in `build-finished` is the only sign; the cases assert it
annoyances.state: open: `blaze why` after a walk that made nothing could say what kept the lane from answering

annoyances.what: `#[rustc_clean(..)]` is refused with rustc's own text (`attribute requires -Z query-dep-graph to be enabled`) and `-Z query-dep-graph` in rustflags is refused too (`blaze does not know which cfgs -Z query-dep-graph decides`), so 88 files of rustc's `tests/incremental` cannot build unchanged under blaze by any setting.
annoyances.cost: an hour: the importer had to write the attributes over with spaces
annoyances.cause: blaze ports the gate of an attribute whose flag it has no meaning for
annoyances.workaround: the importer blanks the six assertion attributes, columns kept
annoyances.state: open: accept the attributes as inert (they assert on rustc's queries), or accept the flag

annoyances.what: A `--cfg` in `.cargo/config.toml`'s `build.rustflags` re-keys the standard library: changing it rebuilt 147 units (`names core`, `link core` ..), about 5 s, where cargo applies rustflags to no prebuilt std. So compiletest's way of flipping a revision tests no reuse at all under blaze.
annoyances.cost: the corpus importer was redesigned to set the cfg from a build script
annoyances.cause: rustflags reach every unit, std's too
annoyances.workaround: a generated `build.rs` that prints `cargo::rustc-cfg` from a file
annoyances.state: open: is std meant to see the workspace's rustflags?

annoyances.what: While four test daemons ran, one build paused with `daemon at 0.1 of 95 GiB (machine 95.0 GiB, 95.1 held by 5 other daemons: pid .. of brv-..-1/h 78.2 ..)`: a daemon serving a two-function crate was counted as holding 78 GiB.
annoyances.cost: none measured; a paused build in a timing-sensitive case
annoyances.cause: not looked into: the store pool's reservation counted as held, or a real footprint under `BLAZE_VERIFY_STORE=1`
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: open: for the daemon-memory lane

annoyances.what: A build log printed whole (`--message-format=json` of a cold build is 60 KB of artifact lines, a `blaze why --all` of one is 230 KB) went into my context twice before every command of mine was piped through a filter.
annoyances.cost: context
annoyances.cause: no default cap on a command's output
annoyances.workaround: filter first; never print a build's JSON
annoyances.state: fixed in my habits

annoyances.what: Fixture texts were generated by a Python script holding Rust in Python strings inside shell heredocs: three rounds of quoting errors (an apostrophe in a cause text ended a string; an old definition later in the script silently overwrote a new one of the same name, so two cases lost a driver).
annoyances.cost: 40 minutes
annoyances.cause: three languages nested
annoyances.workaround: no apostrophes in cause texts; the fixtures are plain files in the tree now, edited there
annoyances.state: fixed: the generator is not part of the tree

annoyances.what: The nix store paths used for `m4`, libclang and glibc's headers were garbage-collected mid-session: the next cold builds of reth and tempo failed in gmp-mpfr-sys (`No usable m4`) and bindgen (`Unable to find libclang`).
annoyances.cost: two wasted 10-25 minute builds
annoyances.cause: fetched by the previous lane with no GC root
annoyances.workaround: `nix build ... --out-link /root/nixroots/<name>` so they are roots
annoyances.state: open: a lane's VM setup should make roots

annoyances.what: A build script may only link from `<HOME>/.blaze/native`, so with one HOME per project and compiler build the LLVM blaze unpacked under `/root/.blaze/native` was refused (`sandbox: link-dir`) for reth's llvm-sys.
annoyances.cost: one failed reth build and a copy step in every run script
annoyances.cause: the native store is per home; nothing shares a layout between homes
annoyances.workaround: `cp -al` the layout into each home's `.blaze/native`
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: nix's libclang has no default include path: bindgen failed with `'assert.h' file not found` until `BINDGEN_EXTRA_CLANG_ARGS` named glibc's and clang's include directories.
annoyances.cost: one failed build
annoyances.cause: an unwrapped libclang
annoyances.workaround: set it in the fixed environment
annoyances.state: open: belongs in the lane setup

annoyances.what: Three cold builds at once (tempo, reth, a copy of reth), each with a 200 GB ceiling, drove the 251 GB VM to 225 GB used; every daemon sat `over the limit` with 0 of 62 workers busy for about 20 minutes.
annoyances.cost: about 25 minutes
annoyances.cause: each daemon sees the others only as pressure
annoyances.workaround: one big build at a time
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: Tests that had never compiled under cargo (`hir-ty-codegen` wasm lowering tests, `blaze-link` `tests.rs:1797`, a duplicate call in `blaze-macro-eval`'s wasm tests) and a control that failed since it was written (`the_oracle_catches_a_given_crate_whose_root_runs_again_only_for_its_log`).
annoyances.cost: a detour in four fixes
annoyances.cause: landed by lanes that could not build or run them
annoyances.workaround: fixed each where met
annoyances.state: fixed where met; unrun tests landing is open

annoyances.what: A unit from `systemd-run` has an empty PATH, and its end kills the blaze daemon the script started (same cgroup), so the next command met a cold daemon; a unit name reused while that daemon lives is refused.
annoyances.cost: a failed first run and several cold restarts
annoyances.cause: systemd's defaults
annoyances.workaround: `export PATH` first; `-p KillMode=process`; a unique unit name per run
annoyances.state: open: vm.sh could do this

annoyances.what: `git diff` printed a rendered diff, not a patch (an external diff tool is configured): shipping it to the VM gave `No valid patches in input`.
annoyances.cost: one failed experiment
annoyances.cause: the user's `diff.external`
annoyances.workaround: `git diff --no-ext-diff`
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: tempo-contracts' body check spent more than 15 minutes on one worker in `unresolved_method_call::similar_candidate` (a probe over every trait per unresolved call, 0.2-1.1 s each) for diagnostics the build then did not print.
annoyances.cost: a 30 minute build in place of 13
annoyances.cause: the suggestion is computed before it is known the diagnostic is kept
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.what: After a cold build of reth-node-ethereum's closure in a copy of reth, one edit of `snap/run.rs` and a build on b0a935736e panicked in dozens of units: `deps/signatures/key.rs:166: module ... vec of an item is not in its crate's def map` and `nameres.rs:1074 ModuleId not found in ModulesMap`. The same loop on a small tokio fixture is fine.
annoyances.cost: stopped the reduction of two reth errors by editing, and the incremental measurements
annoyances.cause: not known when written; the lane's report says what the tree before the merge does
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.where: the measuring binaries from a cargo build
annoyances.what: `target/release/blaze` is blaze-engine's second binary, not the thin client (`blaze-thin`). A bin directory made of `blaze` and `blaze-engine` copied from `target/release` runs the cold build with one daemon and every edit with another: the client sees a daemon of another binary, stops it and starts its own, and the script then fails on the first daemon's pid.
annoyances.cost: three measurement runs, about 25 minutes
annoyances.cause: two binaries named blaze in one directory; the measuring script's header does not say which is which
annoyances.workaround: copy `target/release/blaze-thin` as `blaze`
annoyances.state: open: the script should check that `blaze` is the thin client

annoyances.what: `git diff | ssh ... git apply` sent nothing appliable: the Mac's git has an external diff (difftastic) configured, so `git diff` prints a side-by-side view, and `git apply` says only "No valid patches in input".
annoyances.cost: ten minutes
annoyances.cause: a display setting applies to a pipe
annoyances.workaround: `git diff --no-ext-diff`
annoyances.state: open

annoyances.where: the task's premise: an image served saves memory
annoyances.what: The brief took the dependency images as the mechanism that would make a restarted or warm daemon small. Measured, a restarted daemon is larger than a cold one (6,081 MB against 5,143 MB resident on hello-world): each image is decoded into the same heap values, after the crate was resolved from source anyway (F2), and the first edit after the restart makes 109,000 bodies and 60,000 MIR bodies again (R7).
annoyances.cost: the first plan (serve the images sooner and the memory follows) would have bought seconds and no megabyte
annoyances.cause: nothing measured the restarted daemon's memory before; measure.py had no restart row
annoyances.workaround: measure.py has restart rows now (first no-op, first edit, memory after)
annoyances.state: the rows are in /tmp/records-1111/measure.py; the script is not in the tree (open)

annoyances.what: Letting go of the unread values of every durable row at a build's end (every function, not only `lru` ones; sound through the `keep` path) freed 110 MiB of live heap and not one MB of resident memory, and made each build's end 15 ms longer (`unread values` 1.1 ms to 16.4 ms median, a walk of 2.3 million rows). Built, measured, taken out.
annoyances.cost: two hours
annoyances.cause: freed blocks share mimalloc pages with live ones, so nothing goes back (docs/memory-footprint.md says so of codegen; it holds for query values too); the query storage line in serve.log counts live bytes, which is not what the daemon weighs
annoyances.workaround: only whole arrays, regions and pool pages can go back; values have to be records in pool pages to count
annoyances.state: recorded in restore.md; the patch is /tmp/records-1111/tried-durable-value-eviction.patch on the Mac

annoyances.cost: a look at each run's one failure
annoyances.cause: a test reading process-wide state another test writes; not looked into further
annoyances.workaround: none

annoyances.where: the task's premise: a library's rows are durable
annoyances.what: The brief and blaze-query's docs say library inputs are `HIGH` and a durable row is current without walking its edges. On hello-world 181,865 of 2,105,574 rows are at `HIGH`; 1,906,504 are at `MEDIUM`, because std's rows read inputs of kind `MEDIUM` (the maintainers' `Resolutions` and `ImplSlices`, the crate graph after a change, files' source roots, crate attributes). The first version of shedding durable readers from the reverse index took 64,000 of 2.9 million readers.
annoyances.cost: one build and measurement that bought nothing, an hour
annoyances.cause: nothing reported rows by kind; a row's kind is the lowest it read, and one shared table of kind `MEDIUM` lowers every reader
annoyances.workaround: the pack's span says rows_low, rows_medium, rows_high now; the shed is from `MEDIUM`
annoyances.state: open: a library crate's published tables should be inputs of their own at `HIGH` (restore.md, step 2)

annoyances.where: blaze: the build after a cold build
annoyances.what: The second build after a cold one folds 1.5 million runs into the reverse index at its first view boundary, 390 to 540 ms on the edit's path (`reverse edges fold`, runs=1498483): the runs are the cold build's store of its dependencies' signatures (`store kept front end`), made after the answer and left for whoever opens the next view.
annoyances.cost: about half a second of the second edit, on every binary measured, the base included
annoyances.cause: edges are folded at a view boundary, and the last runs of a build have no boundary after them
annoyances.workaround: none; while the index is shed the fold skips durable rows (150 ms for the same runs)
annoyances.state: open: the task that stores the kept front end should fold what it ran (a fold with `&mut` at its end)

annoyances.what: Before a started daemon listens it syncs the profile history (`profile fsync`), and that one sync took 0.13 to 1.34 s across runs of the same binaries on one VM. The first request after a restart was 3.9, 3.9, 4.1 s on the base and 5.1, 5.2, 4.4 s on this lane's binary with requests of 3.38 and 3.48 s: the row moves by more than the change under test.
annoyances.cost: three extra runs of each binary, and a restart row that still cannot be compared
annoyances.cause: a sync of telemetry on the path to the first answer (restore.md already counts 0.72 s of it on the Mac)
annoyances.workaround: read the request's own span (`request: read to reply`) and not the client's wall time
annoyances.state: open: the profile history should not be synced before the daemon listens

annoyances.what: A one-line body edit of hello-world allocates and frees about 95 MiB of the global heap: `CompiledFunction::clone` 27 MiB, the linker's `file::fill` 20, `Build::patch_lists` 13, `beside::DebugWrite::apply` 8, `codegen::debug_side` 7.5 (alloc_samples by site, eight edits). The warm loop is meant to allocate nothing there (docs/v2/plan/design/memory.md).
annoyances.cost: it is why mimalloc on base pages is 17% slower an edit (each build takes the freed pages again a 4 KiB fault at a time), so it is what keeps 1.0 GiB of huge-page slack on every Linux daemon; and it is edit time on any pages
annoyances.cause: the edit's link and the walk copy whole-program tables
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: mostly fixed on edit2-1111 (2026-11-11): the `Built`'s functions are shared and the `Built` is given back and written into (no clone, no `patch_lists` lists), a patch's place writes the patch (no `file::fill` of the file's runs), the side file is patched by the loop and held once; what is left, about 15 MiB an edit by the samples, is the ELF writer's tables made whole each stage, the store's encoding of the patch, and `Reach::patched`

annoyances.what: `ix new` takes memory only as 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128 or 256 GiB: `--memory 96` is refused (`"96" is not a memory size in GiB`), and the next command (`ix shell`) then fails on a VM that does not exist.
annoyances.cost: a minute; the lane took 128
annoyances.cause: the brief was written from memory of the flag
annoyances.workaround: `--memory 128`
annoyances.state: open: briefs should name a size `ix new` takes

annoyances.where: cargo's target directory: which file is the thin client
annoyances.what: `target/release/blaze` is blaze-engine's second binary, not the thin client: the thin client is `target/release/blaze-thin`, which is installed as `blaze`. The measuring script takes a directory with `blaze` and `blaze-engine`; given the target directory it ran the engine under both names, the second one found a daemon of another binary, stopped it and started its own, and the script died reading `/proc/<pid>/status` of the daemon that was gone.
annoyances.cost: one baseline run (five minutes) and ten minutes finding why the daemon restarted
annoyances.cause: two binaries of one name, and a script that takes a directory
annoyances.workaround: copy `blaze-thin` as `blaze` beside `blaze-engine` into a directory of its own (`/root/install.sh`, gone with the VM)
annoyances.state: open: the measuring script should take the two paths, or check `blaze --version` says thin

annoyances.where: copying blaze's pinned LLVM between two ix VMs
annoyances.what: `ix shell a -- tar -cf - dir | ix shell b -- tar -xf -` through the Mac moved 355 MB in about 20 minutes (0.3 MB/s), and a foreground wait on it is moved to the background after three minutes.
annoyances.cost: 20 minutes before the first build could start
annoyances.cause: the bytes go VM to Mac to VM through two interactive shells; there is no VM-to-VM copy and no fetch of the pinned LLVM by its hash on a fresh VM
annoyances.workaround: started the clone and rustup meanwhile
annoyances.state: open: a lane's VM should fetch the pinned LLVM itself (`blaze` does, cargo's build of blaze does not)

annoyances.where: the tests of all-1111 under cargo, before this lane's changes
annoyances.what: Eight tests fail on the untouched tip of all-1111 (e453ac295a), run in a worktree and a target directory of their own. blaze-codegen: `driver::tests::kept::a_walk_over_kept_describes_builds_what_a_fresh_walk_builds`, the refinement that an edit's `Built` is a fresh build's (`build 1: debug_names differs`: after a function is removed the patched walk still holds it; reproduce with `AXicbYqxDQBACAL/8lZ27r+sJNqQSMEBoZ6UyGKwDWs3wL6Bki+Dv/8GLHwAwg==`). blaze-link: `digest::tests::a_digest_kept_by_updates_is_the_files` (`2 nodes kept, 1 in the file's digest: not canonical`) and `tests::patch::a_same_size_body_edit_writes_the_function_and_a_constant` (`what an edit writes grows with the program`). blaze-cas: `a_changed_byte_in_the_zeros_ending_a_commit_stops_the_store_naming_its_pack`, `a_pack_whose_header_names_another_unit_stops_the_store`, `block_checks::the_oracle_catches_a_head_written_before_its_syncs`, `the_oracle_catches_a_put_reported_durable_that_no_sync_made_so`, `place_crash::the_oracle_catches_a_derived_file_accepted_as_a_crash_left_it`. The codegen one is found by hegel's random draws: it failed in two of three runs of the suite and passed in the third.
annoyances.cost: an hour: a baseline worktree, a second target directory and three test runs to tell them from this lane's changes; and the tree's own promise that an edit builds what a clean build builds is not held by its test
annoyances.cause: not looked for; the codegen one came with or after the edit-work-1111 merge (the test file's last change), the store's with the pool
annoyances.workaround: ran the same suites on the base and compared the lists: the same eight fail there, and this lane's new tests pass
annoyances.state: open: each is its lane's; the codegen refinement is the one that says an edit can build something a clean build does not

annoyances.where: blaze: `blaze explain edit_work` after a `blaze run`
annoyances.what: With no `build=`, `blaze explain edit_work` reads the last build, which after every edit is the `store kept front end` build that follows it and counted nothing: `build 326 counted no work in any stage`. The edit's own build is the one before.
annoyances.cost: a few minutes each time, and a query written by hand to find the build
annoyances.cause: the view's default is the newest build of any kind
annoyances.workaround: `build=N` with N from `select max(build_id) from builds where command like 'run%' and misses > 0`
annoyances.state: open: the default should be the last build that counted work

annoyances.where: blaze: the profile's rows of a link
annoyances.what: The spans of one `unit link` did not line up (`3 spans with no parent row, 26 past their parent`), and 13.7 ms at its end, the `Built` and its 12,000 functions being freed, was under no span: `blaze slow` printed no finding for it. It was found only by grouping the CPU samples by frame (`drop_glue::<CompiledFunction>`).
annoyances.cost: half an hour before the drop was seen at all
annoyances.cause: a value dropped at the end of a task is inside the task's span and under no span of its own
annoyances.workaround: a query over `samples` joined to `spans`, by innermost frame
annoyances.state: fixed for this drop (the `Built` goes back to the driver, edit2-1111); open for the next large drop

annoyances.where: blaze: the daemon's loop on the edit path
annoyances.what: The loop reads a plane task's end every 1 ms (`channel daemon loop: a plane task's end (read every 1 ms)`), so every step of an edit that the loop hands on waits up to a millisecond: `the build's first made unit waits behind the units found kept` is 5.1 ms for hello world's 32 kept units, and a placement's seven effects are seven turns. After this lane the front of a one-function edit (plan 3.7 ms, `plan made: collect the plan's database` 1.8, lower 2 to 6, the kept units 5, changed set and inference 5) is 20 of the daemon's 44 ms.
annoyances.cost: about 10 ms an edit, none of it work
annoyances.cause: a poll where a wake would do
annoyances.workaround: none; not this lane's code
annoyances.state: open: the loop's and the plane's

annoyances.where: blaze: the profile's flush at a build's end
annoyances.what: The profile's flush and its `fsync`s start as the build's request finishes, while the build's outputs are still being renamed onto their paths; on xfs one rename then took 6.6 ms (0.15 ms otherwise), and the answer waits for it.
annoyances.cost: up to 6 ms of an edit's answer, some edits
annoyances.cause: two writers of one file system's log at the moment the answer is due
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: open: the flush could wait for the answer

annoyances.where: blaze-link: what a one-function edit writes
annoyances.what: `.rela.dyn` is rewritten almost whole by a one-function edit of hello world: 303 KB of a 442 KB table in two ranges (`link write` events), because a relocation added or removed moves every one after it. It is 95% of the patch (318 KB), of the store's record of it and of what each path's place writes.
annoyances.cost: about 0.3 MB written three times an edit, and the store's puts are 1.16 MB an edit
annoyances.cause: a table sorted and packed, with no slots that stay
annoyances.workaround: none
annoyances.state: open (the linker's relocations lane): relocations at fixed slots, a gone one left as `R_*_NONE`

annoyances.what: A stage compacted every list of the image (O(image), 14 ms) every seventh edit of hello world: the jump table's cells are one piece whose rebase list names every filled slot, a body edit fills one slot and empties another, and the whole of the last list (12,000 entries) is garbage each time. Nothing said a compaction ran: it was inside `link patch`.
annoyances.cost: 2 ms an edit on average and 14 ms every seventh, seen as `link patch` between 8 and 26 ms
annoyances.cause: one threshold for seven lists, and a list re-pushed whole for one entry
annoyances.workaround: none needed
annoyances.state: fixed on edit2-1111: `link compact` is a span naming the list, and the loader's lists compact alone (a pass over the pieces); open: the cells' rebase list is still made whole by an edit that fills a slot
